title_prefix: P2P nonces, addrman selection and relay
mechanism: CONFIRMED as a shared-stream divergence, with ONE of the finding's cited public sources REFUTED. seed-global-random-state (src/node/entropy.lisp:33-61) installs a single sb-ext:seed-random-state - SBCL's MT19937 - into the process-global CL:*RANDOM-STATE* at the head of init-node (src/node/init.lisp:17). The seed itself is fine: executed, %os-entropy-seed draws 32 bytes from ironclad:*prng*, whose type in the image is IRONCLAD:OS-PRNG (getrandom(2)/urandom), and two calls produced different 253- and 256-bit seeds with *random-state-seed* set. The divergence is the GENERATOR, not the seed. Full grep of src/ for (random / *random-state* gives 34 hits; classified, the ones on the shared global stream are: PUBLISHED ON THE WIRE - the ping nonce (src/networking/peer.lisp:1435, send-ping), the compact-block nonce (src/serialization/messages.lisp:624 and :648, whose two production callers at src/networking/protocol.lisp:2260 and src/validation/block.lisp:2571 both take the (random (expt 2 64)) default), and the sendtxrcncl salt (src/networking/peer.lisp:848); KEPT SECRET - addrman new/tried selection, bucket, position, acceptance probability and the GetAddr shuffle (src/networking/addrman.lisp:425, 508, 520, 521, 527, 532, 575, 595), the addr-relay reservoir (src/networking/protocol.lisp:1100), the addr response-cache jitter (:2630), the Poisson relay timers (:2871 and src/networking/peer.lisp:1329), the feeler/tie-break draws (peer.lisp:1346), the feefilter delay (:1395), the initial-broadcast jitter (protocol.lisp:3205) and the mempool.dat obfuscation key (src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1535). REFUTED: the VERSION nonce is NOT on this stream. src/serialization/messages.lisp:333's (or nonce (random (expt 2 64))) is a default no production caller reaches - both handshake arms set (peer-local-nonce peer) from %fresh-local-nonce (src/networking/peer.lisp:993-1010), which uses (ironclad:random-data 8) and says so, and %send-version-and-capabilities passes it explicitly at :1059. Also bounding: the addrman BUCKET KEY is read from /dev/urandom (src/networking/addrman.lisp:40-49) with the *random-state* path only a fallback, and -txreconciliation is default OFF (src/config.lisp:211), so the salt channel is normally silent. Core draws every one of these from a ChaCha20 FastRandomContext seeded from the OS (refs/bitcoin/src/random.h; AddrManImpl::insecure_rand; PeerManagerImpl::m_rng, deterministic only under the test-only option).
consequence: MECHANISM REAL AND EXECUTED; CONSEQUENCE ARGUED, NOT EXECUTED - S2, not S1. Executed proof that the published and the secret draws are one stream and a deterministic function of its state: re-seeding CL:*RANDOM-STATE* to 12345 and then emitting 0, 1, 2 or 3 ping nonces through the SHIPPED builder shifts everything drawn afterwards - the next addr-relay Poisson interval went 58819434 / 30051426 / 13758240 / 15784290 ticks, the next feeler tie-break 1 / 0 / 2 / 1, the next addrman bucket 129 / 425 / 382 / 546 - and replaying the seed with 2 nonces reproduced (13758240 2 382) exactly. Measured against SBCL's own random-state object, the generator holds 624 32-bit state words and one published 64-bit nonce consumes exactly 2 tempered outputs (a (random 1.0d0) also 2, a small (random 256) 1). MT19937's tempering is a bijection on 32-bit words and its state transition is GF(2)-linear and invertible, so 624 consecutive tempered outputs - 312 published nonces - determine the state in closed form and the generator can be run forwards AND backwards from it; that is a property of the generator, stated as fact, and I did not implement the recovery. What that buys an attacker and what it does not: our node pings every peer every +ping-interval-seconds+ = 120 s (src/networking/peer.lisp:1458), so a peer holding many inbound slots collects nonces fast - 50 slots is ~312 nonces in about 12 minutes - and with the state it would predict which addrman entry is dialled next, when addresses are relayed and when feelers open, which are the inputs an eclipse attacker wants. Three things bound it and are why I do not raise this to S1. (1) The observed nonces are NOT consecutive outputs: every other consumer above draws from the same stream at times the attacker cannot see, so the attacker faces an alignment problem on top of the linear solve, and no probe here shows that problem is solvable in practice. (2) Bucket PLACEMENT stays out of reach - make-addrman-key is /dev/urandom, so predicting selection order does not let an attacker steer addresses into a bucket. (3) The single highest-value published value, the per-connection VERSION nonce, is already on ironclad's CSPRNG, so the one draw an attacker gets from every connection for free carries no state. What remains is nonetheless a genuine 'not a CSPRNG where Core uses one' divergence covering every wire nonce we still publish from it, and it should be closed.
evidence: Executed in the pinned project container (bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4, SBCL 2.6.5.HEAD.1-85913ed) through cl-workbench repl eval. (1) Shared stream, through the shipped builders: (setf *random-state* (sb-ext:seed-random-state 12345)) then N x bitcoin-lisp.serialization:make-ping-message then bitcoin-lisp.networking::%next-exp-interval-ticks / (random 3) / (random 1024) gave N=0 (58819434 1 129), N=1 (30051426 0 425), N=2 (13758240 2 382), N=3 (15784290 1 546); the N=2 triple reproduced exactly on a repeat run. (2) Generator geometry read from SBCL's own object: (sb-kernel::random-state-state st) is a (SIMPLE-ARRAY (UNSIGNED-BYTE 32) (627)) whose element 2 is the MT index; after one (random (expt 2 64)) it read 2, after a make-ping-message +2, after a (random 1.0d0) +2, after a (random 256) +1 - so 624 state words, 2 words per published nonce, 312 nonces to cover the state. (3) OS seeding: two calls to bitcoin-lisp::seed-global-random-state returned different seeds of 253 and 256 bits with *random-state-seed* set, and (type-of ironclad:*prng*) is IRONCLAD:OS-PRNG. Ours: src/node/entropy.lisp:19-61 and src/node/init.lisp:17; the full 34-hit grep of src/ for '(random ' / '*random-state*'; src/networking/peer.lisp:993-1010 (%fresh-local-nonce, ironclad), :1059 (the handshake passes it), :848 (sendtxrcncl salt), :1329, :1346, :1395, :1435 (ping nonce), :1458 (ping interval); src/networking/addrman.lisp:40-49 (OS bucket key), :425, :496-532 (address-book-select), :575, :595; src/networking/protocol.lisp:1100, :2260, :2630, :2867-2871, :3205; src/serialization/messages.lisp:333, :348, :624, :648; src/validation/block.lisp:2571; src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1535; src/config.lisp:211 (-txreconciliation default off). Not on this stream and noted only for completeness: src/storage/txospenderindex.lisp:138-139 draws its SipHash salt from a fresh (make-random-state t), i.e. the clock, and src/node/eviction.lisp:92 is the separate finding 6c83742d. Core: refs/bitcoin/src/random.h (FastRandomContext), refs/bitcoin/src/addrman.cpp (AddrManImpl::insecure_rand), refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp (PeerManagerImpl::m_rng), refs/bitcoin/src/init.cpp:1642 and refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:3369-3379 (per-process nSeed0/nSeed1).
fix_shape: Stop drawing anything an adversary sees, or anything an adversary must not predict, from CL:*RANDOM-STATE*. Follow Core's split rather than replacing the global: introduce one project randomness API backed by a CSPRNG - the tree already has ironclad's OS-PRNG in use at %fresh-local-nonce and make-addrman-key, so a thin bl.crypto layer offering rand64, rand-below(n), rand-double and rand-exp-duration over ironclad is the smallest faithful shape, and it removes the thread-safety problem the %fresh-local-nonce docstring already names (SBCL's *random-state* is not thread-safe and these draws happen on several peer threads at once). Then convert the call sites in two groups. First the values we PUBLISH - the ping nonce (peer.lisp:1435), the compact-block nonce defaults (messages.lisp:624 and :648) and the sendtxrcncl salt (peer.lisp:848) - because a published value from a linear generator is the leak. Second the values we must keep SECRET, matching Core's AddrManImpl::insecure_rand and PeerManagerImpl::m_rng: addrman selection and the GetAddr shuffle (addrman.lisp:425-595), the addr-relay reservoir and its jitter and Poisson timers (protocol.lisp:1100, 2630, 2871, 3205 and peer.lisp:1329), and the feeler and feefilter draws (peer.lisp:1346, 1395). Giving addrman its own context rather than sharing one global is worth copying: it is what makes an addrman draw independent of anything the wire has shown. Leave the mempool.dat obfuscation key and the txospenderindex salt for a separate pass but move them to the OS source too, since neither wants a clock- or MT-derived value. Keep seed-global-random-state and its startup call for whatever non-adversarial uses of CL:random remain, and add a structural test that fails if a new (random ...) appears under src/networking/ or src/serialization/, with a positive control feeding it a synthetic offending form so the ratchet cannot go vacuous. NOT IMPLEMENTED - verdict only.
